A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same DialPrompt research work, with matching main text, figures, tables, Algorithm 1, and Appendices A–D. The five image-based appendix pages were visually inspected and match across versions; no material comparison gaps remain.

before.justification: v1 reports original image-quality experiments, automated user-experience evaluations, a 19-person user study, and ablations in Tables 2–6.

after.justification: v2 retains the original experiments, automated evaluations, 19-person user study, and ablations reported in Tables 2–6.

M1.justification: Both retain the same 15-dimension guidance procedure, GPT-4o dialogue construction, human calibration, and LLaMA3-8B-Instruct fine-tuning with masked user inputs and assistant-response cross-entropy loss.

E1.justification: Both use the same Lexica-derived MTGPD training data, MTGPD60 evaluation set, 200 PartiPrompts examples, and designer, developer, and amateur reviewer populations. No dataset or task coverage changes.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within Tables 2–3 and Appendix D, including PromptGen, PromptExpansion, MagicPrompt, BeautifulPrompt, and the GPT/Claude baselines used in each comparison.

E3.justification: The 9:1 split, 10 training epochs, model configurations, five-turn simulation limit, CLIP/Aesthetic metrics, and user-study procedures are unchanged. Both require at least ten completed dialogues per human reviewer.

E4.justification: Both retain the single-turn versus multi-turn training ablation in Table 5, transfer evaluation across five TIS models in Table 6, and the same ten visualized cases in Appendix D.

E5.justification: Both average two GPT-4o evaluations with assistant order swapped. Neither reports training-seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests; uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables 1–6, Figure 2, and Appendix D retain their results. For example, DialPrompt's Table 2 Aesthetic Scores remain 6.578 and 6.263, and its Table 3 overall user-centricity score remains 7.69.

T1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the same mathematical sets, dimension-difference criterion, and dialogue-construction formulation. No definitions, assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added, removed, or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions concerning 15 prompt dimensions, multi-turn user-centric guidance, and the released dialogue dataset. The headline 5.7% and 46.5% improvement claims are unchanged.

C2.justification: Both retain the explanations linking aesthetics to training-data dimensions and fidelity to multi-turn dialogue, together with limitations concerning linear interaction and insufficient aesthetic richness for professional designers.

D1.justification: Hardware, hyperparameters, data-construction details, and the code/data access link are unchanged. Appendices A–C retain identical templates for dialogue construction, user simulation, and evaluation.

R1.justification: The cited works and positioning relative to existing prompt generators, user-centric AI, and reverse question answering are unchanged. No references or substantive novelty comparisons are added or removed.

P1.justification: The arXiv margin stamp changes from v1 dated 23 Aug 2024 to v2 dated 14 Oct 2025. The prose, terminology, headings, and section/appendix order remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–3, Tables 1–6, and the appendix displays retain their content, captions, structure, and placement. Negligible character-positioning differences do not alter the layout; Appendix D renders identically.

improvement.justification: v2 preserves the scientific content, experimental evidence, reproducibility information, discussion, and appendices of v1. The updated arXiv stamp and negligible rendering differences provide no meaningful improvement or deterioration in the paper's overall quality.
